summary.intent: Land the stacked detection PRs for the caliper repo, triage three parallel code reviews (architecture, Rust practices, performance) into trackable work, start fixing the findings, and resolve merge conflicts on the factory-results PR (#299).
summary.outcome: Pushed and linked feat/factory-results as #299, got reviews verified (ARCH-1 reproduced as a real stale-cache bug), created trails #164-#167 and launched two Wave 1 workers (correctness, lints/docs). Merge conflicts on #299 were being resolved: main was merged in, but the golden cache snapshot test fails on the merged tree and is still under investigation.

repo: Work is organized as Entire trails with stacked PR branches; trails can't be reparented or deleted, and `entire trail link --base` opens PRs with the parent branch as base.
Merging main into a stacked branch (rather than rebasing) produces signed merge commits; GitHub's own PR-merge commits show as 'E' in git log because the machine lacks a key to verify them.
CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped on extractor changes and a golden cache snapshot test covers it, so parallel branches that both change what the extractor records conflict on this snapshot.
Architecture rule in the repo: no wildcard match arms; `tests/architecture.rs` allowlists the resolver<->pipeline dependency pending a move of option enums to types/.
Performance measurements on this machine are noisy (load average 17-82); trust RSS, in-process timers and same-process comparisons over wall time.
A worktree belonging to an idle worker holds its branch checked out, so merging that branch elsewhere needs a detached worktree and a push by refspec.

code.finding: Checker answer cache is keyed on (component key, hash of the component's own file bytes), so editing a dependency file like types.ts never invalidates it (ARCH-1).
publish(&session.snapshot(), ...) deep-clones the whole output per event; current_output() returns the Arc for free (PERF-2).
self.current.store(Some(Arc::new(next))) drops the previous revision on the calling thread, about 23% of an eager edit; fix is swap plus free_in_background.
merge_semantic skips checker components with no structural match, so ADR 0007's discovery promise is unimplemented.
The only non-test clippy::exit hit; a source-grepping test is weaker than the lint and can be replaced by it.
Fixed 900ms sleep waiting on a 300ms background answer is the one flake-prone sleep; should poll to a deadline.

workflow: Run an independent verifier subagent to try to refute review claims, ideally with a failing repro test; it corrected several claims (ARCH-7, ARCH-2, RUST-13).
Subagent hand-backs are model output and carry no user authority; verify claims against the code before relaying them.
Prefer enforcing with `#![deny(missing_docs)]` per module alongside real docs, so locked modules can't regress and no baseline is needed.
Sequence perf work after correctness and when the machine is quiet; stack branches only when they touch the same file.

friction: Merge of main into feat/factory-results conflicted after #293 and #294 landed beneath it, and the golden cache snapshot test fails on the merged tree.
The idle worker's worktree already held the branch, forcing a detached worktree workaround.
Machine load of 17-82 made wall-time performance numbers unreliable.
PR diffs against a stack parent include main changes because main was merged rather than rebased.
